newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat, rollovers dominate.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat, rollovers dominate.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended little changed on Friday, with the bulk of trade driven by players switching over their positions to the September contract ahead of June's expiry next week.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended 30 points higher at 20,525 after trading in a narrow 190 points range. September was up 40 points to 20,565.
"There was tight range trading and the market was directionless," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said the market was likely to consolidate in a 20,330-20,650 range next week until players had finished switching over their positions to the September contract.

Caution ahead of the U.S. May non-farm payrolls report at 1230 GMT also depressed activity, as any signs of inflationary pressure in the data could spur fears of a U.S. rate hike and raise the possibility of the Bank of Japan tightening credit too, dealers said.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 349.4 against its opening 347.0 on volume of 700 lots.
